newsitem.title: SPAIN: Grenades launched at Spain refinery, little damage.
newsitem.headline: Grenades launched at Spain refinery, little damage.

text.p: Two grenades were launched at a refinery in Spain's northern Basque region on Tuesday in what could have been an attack by ETA separatist rebels, police said.
Police said little damage was caused when the grenades exploded around the outer fence of the Petronor refinery in the Basque town of Muskiz during the early hours of Tuesday.
One of the grenades exploded just inside the refinery's boundaries some 50 metres (yards) from a number of oil tanks, while the other landed just outside creating a crater in the earth, police said.
The grenades had been launched from a mountain site 200 metres away.
The attack came just hours before heads of state gathered in Madrid for a NATO summit amid heightened security.

A force of 4,000 police and Civil Guard troops, many wearing body armour and wielding machine guns, have been stationed in key points around Madrid to discourage attacks by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) separatists.
Police fear ETA could be preparing to retaliate for the arrests in the past week of eight alleged members suspected of involvement in the kidnapping of a prison official.
ETA has waged a 29-year violent campaign for an independent Basque state in which 800 people have died.
